slot.In the winter of 1914, the flat: You'd feel the silence of the land all around you.
slot.Here, in the winter of 1914: You'd hardly believe how close the two sides were.
slot.In London, on the evening of the fourth: You'd feel caught up in the excitement, I think.
slot.A trench, in the winter of 1914: You'd never quite get your feet dry, all winter long.
slot.A day in the trenches begins: You'd wrap your cold fingers around the mug and feel a little better.
slot.For many families at home: You'd read every letter until the paper went soft.
slot.On Christmas Eve, the families put up: You'd set an empty place at the table, perhaps, for the one who was away.
slot.On the other side of No Man's Land: You'd find yourself wondering who they were.
slot.When the soldiers come out of the trench: You'd sleep for hours on a pile of straw in a barn.
slot.Just behind the British lines: You'd hear robins singing among the bare branches.
slot.A few days before Christmas: You'd be glad of the hard ground after so much mud.
slot.Christmas morning, 1914, dawns: You'd see the frost sparkling on every blade of grass.
slot.Flanders is peaceful today: You'd hear larks singing over the fields in spring.
slot.On the walls of the Menin Gate: You'd stand very still, with everyone else, until the last note fades.
